To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ito,f, but not Ito,s, is expressed in human LV and is responsible for the notch potential.

Ito,f and its modulation by Kv4.3 channels play a central role in the repolarization of human LV action potentials and that remodeling of Ito,f contributes to AP heterogeneities and prolongation of APs in failing human hearts.

transient outward potassium currents (Ito) are differentially expressed and regulated in the human ventricles, and that these currents are important for the regulation of the action potentials in the human ventricular myocardium.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ito,fast is a major determinant of AP repolarization in human ventricles and its remodeling is a critical factor in cardiac pathophysiology.
Ito,f and/or Ito,s may be potential therapeutic targets for treating human cardiac arrhythmias.
transient outward potassium currents (Ito) have been identified in human left ventricular (human LV) myocytes and play a role in action potential repolarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transient outward currents, particularly Ito,f, are differentially expressed and play a critical role in the repolarization of human ventricular action potentials.
Ito,f and its remodeling are critical for normal and abnormal human ventricular repolarization.
the human left ventricle is a heterogeneous tissue, with different subepicardium and subendocardium action potentials.

the human ventricle expresses two distinct types of transient outward currents, I _{TO,f} and I _{TO,s}, that are differentially expressed and contribute to heterogeneity in AP waveforms in the human ventrucle.
